messages:
jess_newhire: Hey folks, quick q about year-end carryover and a weird case  I'm a contractor converting to full-time on Dec 10. Do I get any front-loaded PTO on conversion or is everything strictly prorated? Also heard about a 40h carry cap  does that apply to people who join late in the year?

maria_peopleops: Congrats on the conversion Jess! :tada: Short answer: we don9t auto front-load on conversion; PTO is prorated based on your conversion date unless you have a special clause in your offer. The 40h carry cap applies to headcount eligible for vacation carryover (FT employees only). Contractors converting to FT mid-year will have an accrual start date of their FT effective date.

jess_newhire: Ok makes sense. If I convert Dec 10 and have 0 vacation hours on that date, can I still carry something into next year if I don't use it?

omar_manager: Our team had a contractor -> FT last year. They were pro-rated and ended up with ~8 hours before year-end, we let them carry the pro-rated amount up to the 40h cap. You should check if your offer included any sign-on PTO credit.

maria_peopleops: To be explicit: policy examples: `annual_alloc = 120h` -> prorated for FT start 12/10: months_employed = 0.67 -> accrued = round(120 * 0.67) = ~80h for the remainder of the year (example only). But pro-rates depend on full/partial month rules in the handbook. Remember carryover: at year-end we automatically roll over up to 40h of unused vacation for FT employees; anything above is forfeited unless a documented exception is approved.

jess_newhire: What about sick time vs vacation? Do either carry?

ryan_hrbp: Sick doesn't carry. Vacation carries up to cap. Also separate state-reqs may mandate different rules (e.g., CA/NY accrual vs carry). We'll follow local law where it overrides.

jess_newhire: If I want an exception (e.g., I couldn't use time due to project blackout), what's the process?

maria_peopleops: Exceptions: manager writes a short justification in the "Carryover Exception" form (link in handbook), attach project blackout dates, and we'll evaluate. Exceptions are rare and approved only for documented business needs. Timelines: submit by Dec 20; decisions by Dec 31.

omar_manager: Also flag any oncall coverage concerns now. If conversion date affects your accrual schedule we should coordinate so you don't lose PTO you'd expect.

peopleops_bot: Policy link: https://intranet.redwood/handbook/leave#carryover (policy v3.4). Reminder: submit Carryover Exception form: https://intranet.redwood/forms/carryover-exception

jess_newhire: Thanks everyone. One small follow-up: is there a grace period for scheduling carried-over hours in Q1? Like must be used by March?

maria_peopleops: Carried hours expire after the first quarter for some locations; for the standard policy carried vacation must be used within Q1 of the following year or it's forfeited, unless an exception is granted. We9ll confirm if your location has special rules and DM you.

peopleops_bot: Ticket created: #CARRY-8812. Assigned: ryan_hrbp. Decision window: 11 business days.

jess_newhire: Appreciate it. Will check my offer letter and submit form if needed. :slightly_smiling_face:
